name: Event-driven services on Kafka
summary: Services that publish facts to Kafka and react to each other's events, with the transactional outbox and change data capture so no event is lost. For domains where many consumers need the same stream of changes.

fitsWhen.says: the data is a stream of events
a system of services reacting to events
the team writes Java, Kotlin or Go

backend.why: Spring for Apache Kafka and Spring Data cover producers, consumers and transactions.

queue.why: A replayable, partitioned log: new consumers can read history, ordering holds per key.

database.why: Each service's state, and its outbox table.

data.why: Change data capture publishes the outbox rows to Kafka reliably.

infra.why: Kafka and the services run as workloads; a managed Kafka removes most of the burden.

ci-cd.why: Build, test, publish images; GitOps for deploys.

observability.why: Consumer lag and end-to-end traces across topics.

testing.why: Integration tests against a real Kafka and Postgres.

hosting.why: A managed Kafka service and managed Postgres.

services.name: orders
responsibilities: Writes state and an outbox row in one transaction

services.name: cdc
responsibilities: Streams outbox rows into Kafka topics

dataStores.name: events
dataStores.purpose: Topics per event type, keyed by aggregate id

environments.name: dev
environments.purpose: docker compose with Kafka (KRaft), Postgres and Debezium

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: Same topology on a small managed Kafka

notes: Topics, partitions and retention defined as code

security.auth: Services authenticate to Kafka with SASL/mTLS; ACLs per topic
security.secrets: Vault or the cloud's secret manager
notes: Events carry no secrets or unnecessary personal data
Retention matches the data policy (GDPR erasure needs a plan)

conventions: Events are named in the past tense (OrderPlaced)
The outbox is written in the same transaction as the state

adrs.title: Transactional outbox with CDC
adrs.decision: Services write events to an outbox table; Debezium publishes them.
adrs.why: Avoids the dual-write problem where the database commit and the publish can disagree.

adrs.title: Kafka as the backbone
adrs.why: Replay and many independent consumers of the same history.
